content.value_statement: Crowded or repetitive interfaces make hierarchy hard to read. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a layout review workflow for spacing, rhythm, and structure.
actual_capabilities: Reviews spacing, hierarchy, grid structure, rhythm, density, and responsiveness.
Creates a layout improvement plan based on spacing systems and content structure.
Recommends Flexbox, CSS Grid, named areas, or responsive grid patterns.
Identifies repetitive card grids, nested cards, equal spacing, and excessive centering.
Uses verification checks for squint test, breathing room, hierarchy, and layout consistency.
limitations: It provides guidance; implementation quality depends on the agent editing the target files.
It assumes existing frontend context and references the frontend-design skill for deeper guidance.
It does not perform automated visual regression testing by itself.
It does not choose brand colors, typography systems, or illustration style as its primary focus.

use_cases.title: Refine a crowded dashboard
use_cases.description: Review a data-heavy screen and identify spacing, hierarchy, and density changes that make repeated use easier.

use_cases.title: Choose CSS layout structure
use_cases.description: Decide when to use Flexbox, Grid, named areas, or responsive columns for a page or component.

use_cases.title: Polish a marketing page
use_cases.description: Break repetitive card sections and create clearer visual rhythm without adding decorative elements.

prompt_templates.title: Review this page layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the arrange skill on TARGET=the current page. Identify the main spacing, hierarchy, structure, rhythm, and density issues before changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Create a spacing plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use arrange for TARGET=the dashboard. Propose a spacing scale, grouping rules, and hierarchy strategy, then apply the smallest needed edits.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor responsive structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use arrange for TARGET=the pricing section. Replace repetitive card-grid structure with a more intentional responsive layout and verify mobile behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a full interface system
prompt_templates.prompt: Use arrange across the app shell and key screens. Normalize spacing tokens, choose layout primitives, reduce nested cards, and document verification results.

output_examples.input: A SaaS dashboard feels crowded and hard to scan.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a prioritized layout plan covering tighter related groups, clearer section breaks, and density changes for repeated use.

output_examples.input: A landing page repeats the same three-column cards in every section.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends varied section structures, asymmetric alignment, and card use only where content is distinct and actionable.

output_examples.input: A component mixes random margins with unclear hierarchy.
output_examples.output: The result standardizes spacing choices, prefers gap for sibling spacing, and verifies hierarchy and responsiveness.

best_practices: Start with content relationships before choosing layout primitives.
Use a consistent spacing scale, then vary density to create hierarchy.
Verify changes at mobile and desktop sizes before judging visual rhythm.
anti_patterns: Do not wrap every group in a card when spacing or dividers are enough.
Do not use equal spacing everywhere; it removes hierarchy.
Do not choose CSS Grid for simple one-dimensional layouts.

faq.question: What does this skill improve?
faq.answer: It improves spacing, hierarchy, structure, rhythm, density, and responsive layout decisions.

faq.question: Does it write frontend code?
faq.answer: It guides the agent to make layout edits when a target project is available.

faq.question: Can it replace a design system?
faq.answer: No. It helps apply or define spacing rules, but it does not replace a complete design system.

faq.question: Does it require another skill?
faq.answer: The instructions reference frontend-design for deeper context and ask the agent to gather design context first.

faq.question: Is it useful for dashboards?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes density and structure checks that suit data-heavy interfaces.

faq.question: Is it limited to CSS Grid?
faq.answer: No. It explicitly compares Flexbox, Grid, named areas, and simpler spacing-based grouping.
